items.A: Rented war chest: the walkaway is the ability to go the distance, to trial rather than settlement, to the tenth week, to the next quarter, and it is supplied by a third party who buys a share of the outcome, as the litigation funder who pays the plaintiff's costs against a slice of the award, or the parent whose guarantee lets a subsidiary refuse a supplier's terms; the carrier is the funding agreement, which the funder holds and the holder does not fully own; keeping it credible costs the funder's slice and the funder's continuing belief in the case; the tell is disclosure, since defendants ask whether a funder exists and some courts now require the answer, and then the terms, since a funder who may withdraw below a settlement threshold owns the walkaway; the fake that survives is the funder disclosed without its terms, so the defendant knows the chest exists and not who may close it; not survival-floors' Accident only, a priced floor from a stranger paid before the fall, since the funder is paid after, and from the win.
items.B: Meter on the walkaway: the option is credible in proportion to a visible quantity that depletes while it is displayed, as the strike fund whose balance the employer divides by weekly strike pay to get weeks, or the mobilized army whose daily cost the neighbor can estimate; the carrier is the fund or the payroll, and in the United States the union's annual filing makes the balance public; keeping it credible costs dues, or the standing cost of the mobilization, paid whether or not the option is used; the tell is the arithmetic, and a counterparty who can read the meter and outlast it waits for it to run down rather than conceding to it, while one who cannot outlast it concedes to the number; the fake that survives is the hidden reserve, a sympathy pledge from another union or an undisclosed credit line, which makes the meter read low on purpose; not runway-illusions' Watched burn, which is the operator's own life repriced by watchers, since here the metered quantity is the threat and the watcher is its target.
items.C: Walk on record: the option is credible because the party has walked before, as the retailer that dropped a national brand for a season and the union that struck once a decade ago, so the counterparty reads the record rather than the present alternative; the carrier is the record, which the party does not control once it exists; keeping it credible costs periodically walking from a deal the party would rather have taken, so the reputation is bought with real losses on a schedule the counterparties set by testing it; the tell is whether any walk is on the record at all and how old the last one is; the fake that survives is the forced exit written up as a chosen one, the deal that died for another reason and reads as a walk, since the record keeps outcomes and not motives; not power-trades' Silence on the tab, a repeated game that prices access, since here the repeated game prices the refusal.
items.D: Pawn-shop option: a real outside option that discredits its holder when shown, as the insider bridge that lets a founder refuse an outside lead's terms and that, once named, tells the lead the outsiders did not come, so a genuine alternative lowers the price it was meant to hold up; the carrier is the counterparty's reading of why the alternative is the alternative; keeping it credible costs silence, since the option is worth most while the counterparty does not know it exists, and its holder must refuse terms without saying what the refusal rests on; the tell is any mention of it, and a counterparty who suspects a bridge asks whether the insiders have already committed; the fake that survives is the unmentioned bridge, which works as a Silent floor until the day it is exercised and becomes a discount; not an option that fails when tested, since this one fails when displayed, and a line that sorts options by whether they must exist has no place for one that exists and must not be seen.
items.E: Ringer: a competing bid is manufactured by a confederate who will not close, as the shill in the auction room whose bids raise the price and who never wins, or the friendly fund that offers a sheet it does not mean to sign so the real lead sees competition; the carrier is the confederate and the conspiracy, and in most auction venues the shill is unlawful; keeping it credible costs the confederate's exposure and the risk that the ringer wins by accident and must be let off, which is the tell, since a ringer's bids never close and a lot the ringer won reappears in the next sale; the fake that survives is the sealed-bid ringer, whose bid is never seen and whose failure to close is never announced; not Paid floor, a real bid bought by contract, since the ringer's bid is real only until it is accepted.
items.F: Nothing to leave: the walkaway is the state the party already stands in, so a company that covers its costs declines a round by doing nothing, and the option needs no counterparty, no paper, and no belief; the carrier is the profit-and-loss statement, which the investor reads in diligence; keeping it credible costs the growth forgone to stay there, so the option is paid for every month in hires not made; the tell is the burn line and whether the company has ever actually chosen the state, since 'we could be profitable by cutting' names a state the company has never stood in; the fake that survives is the cut never made, because the investor cannot see which team would go or whether the product survives their going; not survival-floors' Plot that must be tended, a floor under a person outside any wage, since here the floor is under the firm's refusal and is priced against the round it declines.
items.G: Fed suitor: the alternative is a party with wants of its own, so the second supplier or the rival employer stays an option only while it is given something, a share of the volume, a real chance at the position, and stops quoting the third time it learns it was the stalking horse; the carrier is the suitor's patience; keeping it credible costs a dual-source tax, the ten or twenty percent of volume placed with the second source at a worse price, or the interviews one actually sits; the tell is how long the suitor has been in place and what it has received, since a second source at zero share for three years is a name and not an option; the fake that survives is the suitor who knows and stays because it is paid to, which is the Paid floor by another door; not Qualified on paper, where the certificate needs no one's consent and decays with the spec, since here the option decays with a person's willingness.
items.H: Silent floor: the option is known to the holder alone and works through what the holder will let die, as the employee whose spouse's income means the job is not necessary, so the counterparty sees a calm it cannot source; the carrier is the holder's own knowledge and the posture it produces; keeping it credible costs nothing, since it is never claimed, but a real floor also changes what the holder accepts while the fake changes only how the holder looks; the tell is the brink, since a party with a real floor lets the deal die there and a party without one folds in the last hour, so a counterparty who can afford one dead deal can sort them; the fake that survives is the rehearsed calm against a counterparty who cannot afford the brink, which is most of them; not negotiator-check-loops' walk-away rehearsal, the holder's inner check, since here the question is what the counterparty reads and at what price it can test.
items.I: Check that tips the rival: a claimed option is protected from verification because verifying it hands the alternative the deal, as the incumbent lead who would call the rival fund to confirm the competing term sheet and by calling tells the rival there is a round worth fighting for; the carrier is the small market in which the check leaks; keeping it credible costs naming the rival, since an unnamed sheet is a rumor and a named one is a sheet the incumbent could check at a price; the tell is the refusal to name, and the name itself when the fund named is one known to issue sheets it does not close; the fake that survives is the named sheet that does not exist, since the check costs the checker more than the concession, and a founder who has read the checker's bill knows it; not Kettle on the hob, which has no paper, since here there is a paper the counterparty could ask to see and chooses not to.
items.J: Kettle on the hob: the alternative is a relationship kept at a temperature, as the acquirer's corporate-development team met every quarter so that 'we have inbound interest' stays true, and each meeting costs the founder a slice of information and gives the acquirer a free look; the carrier is the cadence of contact; keeping it credible costs the leak, since a kettle kept warm is being read, and the acquirer is keeping the founder warm as its own option, so the two parties are each other's walkaway and neither knows which of them is the real one; the tell is depth, whether the acquirer's engineers have looked at the code or only its dealmakers have had coffee, and who proposed the last meeting; the fake that survives is inbound interest that was a form letter, since an investor cannot call the acquirer without telling it there is a deal; not Fed suitor, which is paid in the deal's own currency, a share of volume or an interview actually sat, where the incumbent can count what it lost, since the kettle is paid in information about the holder that the counterparty never sees on any ledger.
items.K: Paid floor: an outside option is bought as a real bid, as the stalking-horse bidder in a bankruptcy sale signs a binding purchase agreement and is paid a break-up fee if outbid, so the seller's walkaway exists by contract before the auction opens; the carrier is the signed agreement and the court-approved fee; keeping it credible costs the fee, a few percent of the price, plus a floor set below where the seller hopes to finish; the tell is the fee's size and the expense reimbursement beside it, since a large fee reveals that nobody expected a second bidder and prices the option the seller had to buy; no fake is needed because the option is real by construction, and its failure is the horse chosen because it would win; not power-trades' Fence around the process, which sells the auction's power to one bidder, since here the seller buys a bidder so that there is an auction at all.
items.L: Absent owner's clock: a deadline whose owner is not at the table cannot be negotiated with the party who is, so the offer from elsewhere that expires Friday and the fund whose investment period ends in June import an urgency the table cannot soften; the carrier is the other party's calendar; keeping it credible costs letting it bind, since a clock named and then quietly extended discounts every clock the party names afterward; the tell is whether any deadline this party ever named was allowed to expire, and a request to see the offer with its date on it; the fake that survives is the clock the counterparty cannot watch expire, a private offer whose extension is never disclosed, which works until the counterparty sees the party still seated after the date; not impasse-inventions' invented deadline, which both sides adopt to share urgency, since here the urgency is owned by someone who was never asked.
items.M: Second table in the square: the walkaway from the private table is a public one, the activist's open letter, the employees' petition, the leak, and it is credible in proportion to an audience that would care and a party that has published before; the carrier is the audience; keeping it credible costs earlier tables, since the audience that would care is built by letters already sent, each of which ended the private negotiation it threatened, so the option is one-shot at any table and its credibility at this one is bought with tables lost before; the tell is whether the audience exists and can hurt, a following, a reporter's number, a prior letter that landed, and a drafted letter shown privately is the tell of a party that would rather not send it; the fake that survives is the audience the counterparty overestimates, since the counterparty cannot poll the crowd before the letter goes; not Higher court's door, which appeals to a superior with jurisdiction, since the square has none and cannot be bought.
items.N: Cheap to claim, ruinous to check: the walkaway destroys both parties, liquidation rather than a down round, the regulator rather than the settlement, the founder who leaves rather than takes the terms, and it is credible in proportion to a small probability of madness times a large loss, so it need not be likely to work; the carrier is the counterparty's estimate of what the holder has done to itself before; keeping it credible costs occasionally doing something ruinous, which is why the reputation is rarely maintained and the threat usually discounted; the tell is whether the holder has ever burned anything of its own, and a counterparty who finds nothing in the record calls it; the fake that survives is the one the counterparty cannot afford to test at any probability, because the concession is smaller than the expected ruin; not a walkaway to an alternative, since there is no alternative and the leaving is the point, which it shares only with Tied hands, where the leaving is an excuse and here it is a threat.
items.O: Option they built for you: the counterparty supplies the option from its own prior, so the founder with the right resume is assumed to hold competing sheets and the surgeon assumed to hold offers, and the holder claims nothing; the carrier is the counterparty's model of the market and of the holder's kind; keeping it credible costs nothing while the prior holds and cannot be bought when it does not, since a claim would invite the check the prior spared; the tell is that there is none, because the counterparty never asks, and the option fails only when the prior updates, a down market, a public failure, a rival who checked; the fake that survives is the whole item, since no fake is manufactured, and a party who learns to look the part has built nothing and holds the strongest untested option on this map; not Silent floor, which the holder knows and the counterparty reads off posture, since here the holder may hold nothing and know it.
items.P: Higher court's door: the walkaway is an appeal to a table above this one, bought from the higher power, as the medieval borough's charter let the town's disputes go to the king's court rather than the lord's, and as an arbitration clause or a regulator's complaint line does now; the carrier is the grant, recorded and paid for; keeping it credible costs the higher party's fee and its continuing interest in having the lower party as a client, so the door closes when the crown stops needing the town; the tell is the record of the grant and whether the door has ever been used; the fake that survives is the forged charter, which monastic houses produced in quantity and which the crown honored often enough when the forgery's side was the side it preferred, so a fake stands as long as the verifier wants it to be real; not register-jumps' carriers, which move a live situation into a new register, since here the jump is only threatened and its credibility is a document in a chest.
items.Q: Qualified on paper: the alternative is proven feasible without being used, as the second supplier whose parts passed qualification lots and sit on the approved-vendor list with no orders, so the incumbent faces a certificate that a switch could be made; the carrier is the qualification record and its date; keeping it credible costs re-qualification every time the specification moves and the second source's line staying tooled, so an unrevised certificate decays as the product changes under it; the tell is the date of the last qualifying lot against the date of the last design change, and whether the second line still exists; the fake that survives is the qualification of a superseded part, which the incumbent cannot check without the customer's revision history; not lead-time-floors' Understudy, a replacement finished and waiting, since the understudy is bought for the day the source dies and the certificate for the day the source is priced.
items.R: Tied hands: unwillingness is converted into inability, as the negotiator whose board will not approve above a figure, the buyer whose policy forbids the term, the ransom negotiator who says the family has already sold the house, so the walkaway is a constraint persuasion cannot reach because its owner is not in the room; the carrier is the constraint's paper or its absent principal; keeping it credible costs consistency, since a party that later finds the money has revealed every future constraint as a choice; the tell is the constraint's edges, since a counterparty who asks for something the constraint does not cover finds that a real constraint yields easily there and a fake one resists everywhere; the fake that survives is the constraint whose owner cannot be reached, a policy nobody can produce, a board that does not meet; not Absent owner's clock, which borrows someone else's date, since this borrows someone else's refusal; and not impasse-inventions' invented principal whose ratification buys distance and delay, a chip both sides adopt to break a deadlock, since here the principal belongs to one side and its refusal is meant to hold.
